text:
jay: Quick heads-up — ran an nsys capture on the TRT->vLLM integration while repro'ing higher p95. Trace shows a lot of time in the scheduler wrapper and smallish engine enqueues. Posting top-lines and commands below, curious if anyone has seen the same pattern.

jay: nsys cmd I used:
```bash
nsys profile -o trt_vllm_nsight --trace=nvtx,cuda,cublas --stats=true --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-start=span:start --capture-range-end=span:end python -m benchmarks.run_repro
```

jay: nsys summary (cut):
```
GPU Activity:  82.1%  Kernel (attention_fwd) 0.6ms x 1200
CUDA API:     10.9%  cudaMemcpy H2D 1.1ms x 420
CUDA API:      7.0%  cudaLaunchKernel wrapper 0.3ms x 5000
Other:        many small nvtx spans labelled vllm::scheduler::dispatch ~3-5ms each
```

natalie: can you attach the perfetto/qt or the nsys report link? want to see timeline (nvtx) — the per-request spans are the key.

sam: from a quick nvprof run I saw repeated patterns:
```
trt_engine::enqueue        3.2ms
vllm_scheduler::dispatch 4.8ms
cudaMemcpy HtoD            1.1ms
attention_fwd_kernel       0.6ms
```

eli: my suspicion: lots of microbatches (bs=1) so enqueue+overheads dominate. also KV cache behavior can blow up sequence lengths when we have cache misses, making tiny wins from TRT kernels. do we have cache hit ratios for this run?

perf-bot: PR #3214 introduced a scheduler change on 2026-02-10 — observed p95 latency +18% in canary for services using TRT wrapper. See metrics dashboard -> perf/regressions/3214.

mike: fwiw, we recently changed the batching heuristic to be greedier about latency vs throughput which can create more small batches. try setting LOG_BATCH_STATS=1 and TRACE_BATCHER=1 env vars to print queue sizes / batch composition.

natalie: also check for accidental stream syncs in the wrapper. I once saw \`cudaStreamSynchronize(stream)\` in a helper that was intended for debugging — that kills async enqueue.

sam: small repro snippet I found inside trt wrapper (pseudo):
```cpp
bool do_infer(...) {
  engine->enqueueV2(buffers, stream, nullptr);
  // BAD: leftover debug sync
  cudaStreamSynchronize(stream);
  return true;
}
```

eli: if that's present, it explains the 3-5ms scheduler span: enqueue returns quickly but sync forces host wait. remove sync and poll differently.

jay: plan proposal: 1) add NVTX spans around scheduler enqueue + engine call, 2) re-run nsys with per-stream capture to confirm sync, 3) collect KV cache hit/miss ratios for the same sessions, 4) try forcing mini-batching (pack bs>1) to see impact.

mike: I ran a quick capture on the staging repro with NVTX injected. result: scheduler spin-wait loop was polling condition and doing tiny sleeps — ~2.9ms per request of pure CPU wait before enqueue. also found one place we call cudaDeviceSynchronize inside error-path logging (ugh).

natalie: thanks — can you paste the nvtx timeline snippet? small SVG would help but a line summary is fine.

mike: timeline lines (condensed):
```
[00:00.000] nvtx:scheduler:prepare_batch 0.2ms
[00:00.200] nvtx:scheduler:wait_for_ready 2.9ms  <-- spin/sleep loop
[00:03.100] nvtx:wrapper:trt_enqueue 0.15ms
[00:03.250] nvtx:cudaMemcpy H2D 1.1ms
[00:04.400] nvtx:kernel:attention_fwd 0.6ms
[00:04.980] nvtx:wrapper:post_process 0.1ms
```

sam: that wait_for_ready is high — maybe our batch timeout or readiness check granularity is too coarse. we can reduce the sleep backoff steps to lower p95 at cost of some CPU.

eli: KV cache stats: for this run cache_hit=72%, miss=28% which increases average sequence length by ~22 tokens (more work in attention kernel) but doesn't explain the 2.9ms poll. cache issues are secondary.

jay: agree. root cause looks like a combination: 1) scheduler polling/backoff causing ~3ms per req, 2) occasional syncs in wrapper/error paths adding host stalls, 3) small microbatches making enqueue overhead significant.

mike: I pushed a small branch reducing spin backoff + removed a leftover sync in wrapper. I'll run AB test tomorrow. branch: fix/scheduler-spin-and-sync.

natalie: also let's add automated checks: NVTX span coverage in unit/integration tests and a CI nsys probe that fails if wrapper adds >0.5ms extra per call on baseline.

sam: for measurement: recommend these commands:
```bash
# run with NVTX regions from code
nsys profile -o trt_vllm_debug --trace=nvtx,cuda --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-start=span:sched_start --capture-range-end=span:sched_end python -m repro.script
# quick per-kernel timings
nvprof --print-gpu-trace --csv python -m repro.script
```

jay: great. I'll log follow-ups in the perf ticket and attach the nsys report. thanks all :thumbsup:

mike: will post AB numbers tomorrow after the branch run.

eli: if AB looks good we should backport to the release branch (Dedicated + Private customers are sensitive to p95).

perf-bot: noted — created issue PERF-4827 to track fixes and regression tests.
